title: East-West regional fallback repro notes (scratch)
content:
Purpose
- Quick scratchpad for reproducing the intermittent east->west regional fallback that surfaced 2025-10-30. Not a polished postmortem — steps and observations for next-day pairing with SRE.

Summary of symptom
- Production requests from region `us-east-1` are sometimes routed to `us-west-2` fallback tier for ~5–30s bursts even when us-east capacity is nominal. Client latency spikes (p95) and KV-cache miss ratios increase during these bursts.
- Appears correlated with short-lived control-plane re-evaluations of route weight when a single node reports transient health jitter.

Hypothesis (current)
1) Smart-routing jitter: control-plane marks a connection as degraded on a very small error rate (>0.5% over 10s window) and triggers immediate fallback to regional variant with no hysteresis; but the degraded mark propagates to routing decisions before the node recovers, causing oscillation.
2) KV-cache affinity lost on fallback: when routed to fallback region the request loses hot prefix KV, leading to cache misses and higher server-side latency, which in turn reinforces the degraded signal (feedback loop).
3) Edge egress path flapping (BGP briefly shifting) occasionally causes ~200ms jitter that looks like degraded health to the probe logic.

What I ran locally (repro attempts)
- Environment: my laptop (macOS) to control test client, test cluster: staging-eu -> staging-us-west replication enabled. Tried to simulate error windows.

Commands / traces
1) Observe routing decision logs (on control-plane replica cp-03):
$ sudo journalctl -u redwood-control -f --since "2025-10-30 03:00" | rg "route-decision" -n
2025-10-30T03:12:34Z route-decision: request_id=abc123 src=us-east-1 target=us-east-1 score=0.97
2025-10-30T03:12:35Z route-decision: request_id=abc124 src=us-east-1 target=us-east-1 score=0.94
2025-10-30T03:12:36Z route-decision: request_id=abc125 src=us-east-1 target=us-west-2 score=0.41 reason="node-health:node-12 jitter"
2025-10-30T03:12:36Z route-decision: request_id=abc126 src=us-east-1 target=us-west-2 score=0.39 reason="fallback-weight-exceeded"

Note: timestamp cluster shows immediate switch at 03:12:36. The control-plane logs show node-12 jitter flagged; yet node-12 health probe returned OK 2s later.

2) Health probe output against node-12 (from cp-03):
$ curl -sS http://10.12.128.12:8080/health | jq .
{
  "status": "ok",
  "kv_cache": {
    "hit_rate_p95": 0.996
  },
  "uptime": 108864
}

But probe logs show a 502 window 03:12:35–03:12:36: server returned 502 on internal /probe HTTP due to a short upstream read timeout.

3) tcpdump on node-12 during the window (short capture):
03:12:35.214 IP client->node12: GET /v1/generate
03:12:35.216 IP node12->upstream: SYN
03:12:35.219 IP node12->upstream: RST
03:12:35.220 IP node12->client: 502 Bad Gateway

Interpretation: upstream ephemeral connection reset (RST) caused probe failure and a single 502 — enough to flip routing score per current threshold.

Commands tested to reproduce/force behavior
- Force a single node RST via iptables to emulate upstream flapping:
$ sudo iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp --dport 443 -m statistic --mode random --probability 0.003 -j REJECT --reject-with tcp-reset
- Restart probe service and watch cp logs. When we injected ~0.3% resets we observed route-eject events within 15–30s.

- Query routing decision API to inspect threshold math:
$ curl -sS "http://cp-03.internal:9000/debug/route?src=us-east-1&policy=smart&verbose=1" | jq .
{
  "score": "0.41",
  "contributing_factors": ["node-health:node-12:jitter=0.67","kv-miss=0.22","latency=0.11"]
}

Design / policy notes observed
- Current smart-routing config: immediate fallback if node-health component lowers score < 0.5 for any node in set. No minimum consecutive-window enforcement.
- Fallback routing does not preserve KV affinity tags (we attach per-region KV-cookie that is not forwarded across region fallback).
- Canary/auto-fallback has a soft cooldown of 60s globally but that only prevents model variant swapping, not per-request routing decisions.

Repro recipe (minimal)
1) On staging cluster, identify a healthy node (node-12) behind regional pool east-1a.
2) Inject upstream connection resets (iptables or tc) at ~0.2–0.5% probability to create intermittent 502s for ~30–60s.
3) Tail control-plane routing logs and spot route-decision changes.
4) Confirm affected requests are sent to us-west-2 and measure KV-hit-rate pre/post.

Observed numbers (staging run 2025-10-31):
- baseline KV-hit p95: 0.995
- during bump: KV-hit p95: 0.61
- route-decision flips per-min: 8–12 during a 2-minute injection window
- request latency p95 increased from 75ms -> 320ms on fallback flows

Quick mitigation ideas (tested locally)
- Add hysteresis: require degraded score < 0.5 for two consecutive 10s windows before routing switch. Reduced flips to near-zero in sim.
- Preserve KV-affinity: attach region-affinity cookie and, when falling back, try to prefer nodes that can proxy/forward KV prefix (requires proxy work).
- Increase probe smoothing / use EWMA with larger alpha so single reset does not immediately drop node-health to failing.
- Emergency soft-force: tweak routing weight for us-west-2 to +0.05 to reduce full cutover while we patch probes (bad, but quick).

Things I did NOT try (need to):
- Reproduce with real cross-AZ BGP flaps (requires networking coordination).
- Validate whether the control-plane decision is based exclusively on node-level probe or includes aggregated per-pop metrics (log hints show node-level flagged).
- Confirm whether fallback path preserves TLS session resumption (could be additional latency source).

Open questions / action items
- [ ] Pair with SRE (Rosa) to validate infra-level egress jitter (bgp / transit).
- [ ] Add regression test to simulate 0.2–0.5% RST traffic and assert no route-eject for 60s windows. Link test in GH PR.
- [ ] Draft config change: require 2 windows of degraded health OR combine node-health + sustained kv-miss > 0.25 to trigger fallback. (Write as RFC change request).
- [ ] Postmortem stub (INF-4521) — add timelines and impact numbers.

Notes-to-self
- When writing RFC, include diagrams: control-plane scoring flow, failover hysteresis, KV-affinity token lifecycle.
- Keep reproducer script handy: scripts/repro/east-west-flip.sh (local only, not yet in repo).

Raw snippets for easy copy
- route decision debug API (one-liner):
curl -sS "http://cp-03.internal:9000/debug/route?src=us-east-1&policy=smart&verbose=1" | jq .
- quick iptables injection (undo with -D):
sudo iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp --dport 443 -m statistic --mode random --probability 0.003 -j REJECT --reject-with tcp-reset

End of scratch notes. Will convert to an infra playbook once next steps validated with SRE.
